alt_text: Late-afternoon view of Seville's Plaza de España, with its curved brick Renaissance Revival building, tiled alcoves, canal, fountain, and tower, and a few people strolling across the paved square. in Barrio Santa Cruz, Seville. Text on the image: Write a stronger first line
caption:
Most emails, reports and proposals lose their reader before the second sentence. The first line does the heavy lifting. Before: "I am writing to let you know that we have had some delays with the project." After: "The launch will be two weeks late. Here is the new plan." The second version starts in the middle of the action, makes one clear promise (a plan) and drops the warm-up. Nothing is lost, and the reader knows exactly why to keep going. A quick test: read your opening line aloud. If you hear yourself clearing your throat, cut it and start where the real message begins.
